newsitem.title: USA: ADAC terminates dividend to fund growth.
newsitem.headline: ADAC terminates dividend to fund growth.

text.p: ADAC Laboratories Inc, a supplier of radiology and laboratory information systems, said Monday it would stop paying its $0.12-a-share quarterly dividend and channel the funds toward company growth.

"There are a number of growth opportunities internally and through acquisitions," David Lowe, chief executive, said in a statement. "Shareholder value (can) be enhanced in the short run and long term by reinvesting our corporate funds."
ADAC also announced an initial step toward that goal by signing an agreement to acquire Geometrics, a software developer and ADAC's partner in radiation therapy planning.

The acquisition is valued at about $3.9 million, ADAC said. Geometrics makes specialized medical software used in planning radiation therapy treatments for cancer. It has developed the core software for ADAC's Pinnacle3 three-dimensional radiation oncology planning system.
Geometrics will operate as the product development unit of ADAC's Radiation Therapy Planning division.

Earlier, ADAC reported earnings for the fiscal 1996 fourth quarter of $0.26 a share versus $0.16 a share for the year-ago period. ADAC generated a record $64.9 million of revenue, a 29 percent increase from $50.2 million the corresponding period last year.

ADAC reported strong demand for its Molecular Coincidence Detection (MCD) technology and new laboratory and radiology information systems in the fiscal year. MCD bookings rose from five units in the third quarter to 22 in the fourth quarter.
